ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Seven cookies of radius $1$ inch are cut from a circle of cookie dough, as shown. Neighboring cookies are tangent, and all except the center cookie are tangent to the edge of the dough. The leftover scrap is reshaped to form another cookie of the same thickness. What is the radius in inches of the scrap cookie?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a large circular piece of dough, inside which 7 identical small circular cookies have been cut out; one small circle is in the center, and the other 6 small circles are arranged around it in hexagonal symmetry. In the figure, adjacent small circles are tangent to each other, and the 6 small circles in the outer ring are also all tangent to the boundary of the large circle. Reasoning: The radius of each small cookie is 1 inch. Any one cookie in the outer ring is tangent to the center cookie, so the distance from the center of the large circle, that is, the center of the center cookie, to the center of that outer-ring cookie is 1+1=2. That outer-ring cookie is also internally tangent to the large circle, so the radius of the large circle equals this distance plus the radius of the outer-ring cookie, namely 2+1=3. The area of the large circle is 9π, and the total area of the 7 small cookies is 7π, so the remaining scrap area is 9π−7π=2π. Remaking the scraps into a circular cookie of the same thickness, let its radius be r, then πr²=2π, therefore r²=2, r=√2.

From the text, use that each small cookie has radius 1, neighboring cookies are tangent, and all six outer cookies touch the dough edge. Since an outer cookie is tangent to the center cookie, the distance from the center of the dough/center cookie to any outer cookie center is 1+1=2. Since that same outer cookie is internally tangent to the dough circle, the dough radius is 2+1=3. Then compute leftover area as area of large circle minus area of seven unit circles: 9π−7π=2π. Equate this to the area πr² of the reshaped scrap cookie, giving r²=2 and r=√2.

claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: The distance from the center of the large circle, that is, the center of the center cookie, to the center of that outer-ring cookie is 1+1=2

claims.claim: The radius of the large circle equals the distance from the center to the center of an outer-ring cookie plus the radius of the outer-ring cookie.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: The radius of the large circle equals this distance plus the radius of the outer-ring cookie

claims.claim: The radius of the large circle is 2+1=3.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: That is, 2+1=3

claims.claim: The area of the large circle is 9π.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: The area of the large circle is 9π

claims.claim: The total area of the 7 small cookies is 7π.
claims.label: reasoning

claims.claim: The remaining scrap area is 9π−7π=2π.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: So the remaining scrap area is 9π−7π=2π

claims.claim: Remake the scraps into circular cookies of the same thickness.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Remake the scraps into circular cookies of the same thickness

claims.claim: Let the radius of the circular cookie made from scraps be r.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Let its radius be r

claims.claim: The circular cookie made from scraps satisfies πr²=2π.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Then πr²=2π

claims.claim: r²=2。
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Therefore r²=2
